newsitem.title: UK: INSIGHT-Gold needs to tackle upside or face losses.
newsitem.headline: INSIGHT-Gold needs to tackle upside or face losses.

text.p: SPOT NY CLOSE * SUPPORT * RESIST * RSI14 * MA10 * MA30
-----------------VIEWS FROM THE MARKET - April 22-------------
Gold is moving sideways but needs to regain $345 an ounce resistance soon if prices are to advance, analysts said. Silver faces a similar scenario.
Platinum's prospects are brighter after last week's jolt to the upside, with a breach of $385 resistance seen possible.
GOLD - Prices have been moving sideways after last week's dip below $340 and need to push higher in order to avoid another push to the downside, analyst said.
"Gold needs to regain and maintain a foothold over the $345.00 level in order to make any impact to the upside," said technical analyst Karen Jones of Credit Suisse First Boston.
"What that would do is alleviate downside pressure and at least suggest that it will hold sideways rather than go down," she added.
At 0800 GMT spot gold was indicated at $341.75/$342.25 per ounce.
SILVER - Prices have held sideways for about two weeks after falling to around $4.65 and, like gold, silver needs to make a break higher soon to maintain its equilibrium, analysts said.
"It's holding sideways. It's not producing a bounce from the $4.60 area which leaves it under pressure," Jones said.
"I continue to watch $4.85, the high from last week, which if regained could seen silver start basing and then move on to $5.00."
But failure to hold above the $4.60 area would signal a sell off to $4.33, Jones noted.
At 0800 GMT spot silver was indicated at $4.74/$4.76 per ounce,
PLATINUM - Chartwise, platinum was consolidating just below $385 resistance, but its rosy technical pressure showed no downside pressure and plenty of upside potential, Jones said.
"Once it takes that out, and I think it will, it will target $390 and then $400," she said.
The market was still jittery and closely watching for fresh news regarding delayed Russian supplies of platinum group metals, dealers said.
At 0800 GMT spot platinum was indicated at $380.00/$381.00
--Lida Poletz, London newsroom +44 171 542 2936
